<reason>CON won a close, high-quality clash by forcing an apples-to-apples comparison: once caps and housing/retail rules are shared tools, spreading still had to justify extra footprint, enforcement, and possible added trips. PRO was vivid on fairness and land-use conversion, but often compared well-regulated dispersal to an inadequately capped “sacrifice zone,” which CON neutralized. After that, CON’s decision rule—residents feel actual pressure, not their share of sightseeing—was the cleaner reason to reject spreading as the required remedy.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Rebuttal 2 equal-standards attack: if original hosts remain overwhelmed, tighten the cap; do not call a weak cap “protective” and then use its failure to prove dispersal necessary.</best_rebuttal>
